items.title: Add file-like pager: `click.get_pager_file()`

labels.body: The fallback path for an empty `cmd_parts` hard-codes the encoding as `"utf-8"`. If this ultimately writes to a real stdout stream with a different encoding, `get_pager_file` will wrap `stdout.buffer` with UTF-8 and emit bytes in the wrong encoding (mojibake). Use `get_best_encoding(stdout)` (or avoid re-wrapping stdout at all) so the encoding matches the actual stream.

`click.get_pager_file` is a new public API, but there don't appear to be tests covering it (only `echo_via_pager`). Adding a small test that writes to the returned file (including ANSI stripping behavior and the cmd-not-found/nullpager paths) would help ensure the new pager refactor doesn't regress across platforms.

`MaybeStripAnsi` subclasses `io.TextIOWrapper` directly and doesn't implement the non-closing behavior Click uses elsewhere (`_NonClosingTextIOWrapper.__del__` detaches to avoid closing shared global streams). Because `get_pager_file` creates short-lived `MaybeStripAnsi` wrappers around things like `sys.stdout.buffer`, when the wrapper is garbage-collected it can close the underlying stream / fd,
